issues.description: SealSaloon.orders is specified in the problem statement as a modifiable "List<Meal>" (order queue), but the solution implements it as an array "Meal[] orders". This type mismatch can confuse students about the expected data structure for FIFO handling and about which operations/APIs (List vs array helpers) they are supposed to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the specification and reference implementation: either (a) change the problem statement/UML to explicitly allow an array-based queue (Meal[]) and mention ArrayHelpers usage, or (b) change the solution to use List<Meal> (e.g., ArrayList) for orders and adjust FIFO removal accordingly.

issues.description: The problem statement requires SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery and SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice to be static, but the provided example usage in the template Main calls them as instance methods (shop.acceptSupplyDelivery(...), shop.calculateTotalPrice(...)). This inconsistency makes it unclear to students whether these APIs must be implemented as static or instance methods.
issues.suggestedFix: Update Main's example calls to use the class name for static methods (SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery(...), SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice(...)). Alternatively, if instance methods are intended, remove the 'must be static' requirement from the problem statement and adjust the UML accordingly.
